symptom: `describe module M with all` on a module of 229 microflows hit `statement timed out` after 5 minutes; with MXCLI_EXEC_TIMEOUT=40m it stopped at `output line limit exceeded (10000 lines) ... statement aborted`, truncated mid-flow
cause: Three things. (1) The default 5-minute wall-clock guard and (2) the fixed 10,000-line output guard, both meant for runaway statements, applied to a dump that is bounded by the module. (3) The time: describing a microflow derives its layout by rebuilding it (`derivedFlowLayout` → `buildMicroflowFromStmt` → `microflowsNamed`) with `ctx.Backend` swapped for `layoutCheckBackend`, which embeds the `FullBackend` interface and so hid the modelsdk backend's optional `microflowLookup`; `microflowsNamed` fell back to `ListMicroflows`, decoding every microflow of the project once per described flow — quadratic in the module, linear in the project
insight: Lifting the limits alone would have turned a timeout into a 40-minute success. The cost was found by CPU profile, not guessed: 63% of a 229-flow dump in `ListMicroflows` → `codec.Decode` under `derivedFlowLayout`, while the unit-file read count (2069 → 369 with a statement-scoped `CacheUnitReads`) moved wall time not at all — reads were not the cost. A wrapper that embeds an interface drops every optional capability of what it wraps: any `ctx.Backend.(X)` check inside the span silently takes the slow fallback, and nothing fails. Grep the type assertions against `ctx.Backend` whenever the backend is swapped for a decorator. Guard with a count (full listings per dump < flows, via a counting backend that embeds the concrete `*modelsdkbackend.Backend` so it keeps the optional lookups) and prove output unchanged: the 229-flow dump is byte-identical to main's. Real binaries on pedapp + 400 flows: 66.9 s exit 1 at 10,025 lines → 5.7 s, 12,810 lines
